messages.subject: Redline renewal - discount level needs review before contracts go out
messages.body:
Dear Marta,

I am escalating this because time is short: Tomás has offered Redline a 15% discount on a 2-year renewal, citing verbal approval. I have found no written approval, and 15% sits well above the 5% ceiling that sales may approve independently.

The financial effect is not cosmetic. Redline represents roughly 18% of our revenue, and a 15% concession on that base pulls our blended gross margin below the 68% floor we agreed with the board in November. I have modelled it: at 15% we land at approximately 65.8%; at 10% we stay at 68.4%, just above the floor.

May I gently suggest we cap the discount at 10% on a 2-year term before the contract reaches Bruno? Once it is signed at 15%, it is locked for two years.

Kind regards,
Helen

Helen Oyelaran | Chief Financial Officer | Parcelwise B.V.

messages.body:
10 max. 2-year term. we don't go under the 68% floor, not even for redline.

tomás — new paper today, before bruno signs anything.

Sent from my iPhone

messages.subject: RE: Redline renewal - discount level needs review before contracts go out
messages.body:
Marta, Helen,

I have to be honest, this puts me in a very awkward spot with Bruno. He has the 15% offer in writing from Monday, he was already flexing about it on our call, and walking it back 5 points two days later makes us look like we don't know our own numbers ⚠️

Also, for the record, I would never have sent it if I thought the corridor conversation wasn't approval. My fault for not getting it in writing, noted, but the damage risk here is real — Redline is exactly the account RouteBee is circling.

Can we at least meet in the middle at 12%? 🙏

Tomás

messages.subject: RE: Redline renewal - discount level needs review before contracts go out
messages.body:
no. 10.

if bruno pushes, offer the v3 pilot seat and the driver-app training hours instead. that costs us nearly nothing and he values it. call him yourself, today.

Sent from my iPhone

messages.subject: Redline renewal - one correction to Monday's offer
messages.body:
Hola Bruno,

Quick correction before anything goes to signature, and I would rather you hear it from me directly: the discount number in Monday's email should have been 10%, not 15%. That was my error in the draft — apologies, it was sloppy of me.

Here is what I can do to make the 2-year deal properly attractive at 10%: you get the dedicated v3 pilot slot from April 20 (your drivers on the new app months before general release), plus a full training programme for your dispatch team at no charge, plus price protection for the entire term.

Honestly, Bruno — the pilot alone is worth more than the 5 points. Can we get on a call Thursday or Friday and close this properly?

Saludos,
Tomás

messages.subject: RE: Redline renewal - one correction to Monday's offer
messages.body:
Tomás,

You quoted 15% in writing on Monday and it is 10% on Wednesday. Which number is real? If your own pricing needs two versions in 48 hours, forgive me for wondering what happens mid-contract.

I will look at the pilot argument, but I am not signing anything this week. Send the corrected paper and I will review it when I review it.

Bruno Alvarez
COO, Redline Couriers

messages.subject: RE: Redline renewal - discount level needs review before contracts go out
messages.body:
Dear all,

For completeness: the corrected contract will state a 10% discount on a 2-year term, which keeps us at 68.4% blended gross margin, above our floor. I will check the figures line by line before anything is sent to Bruno, so there are no further corrections.

The pilot and training concessions are cost-light and do not affect the margin calculation.

Kind regards,
Helen

Helen Oyelaran | Chief Financial Officer | Parcelwise B.V.
